findings.title: Mode E: dek_commit continuity for acl/service-rekey is unverifiable without a key; a wrong-M record wedges every replica
findings.detail: R4's rationale ('dek_commit continuity is how a verifier without a key knows an acl epoch re-wrapped the same M') is false. The DLEQ proves all listed recipients recover ONE M; nothing links that M to the head's M. Any admin (every admin knows M; a buggy client suffices) builds kind=acl with a fresh M', a valid batched proof over M', and dek_commit copied from head. A keyless verifier passes E1-E4, C1-C4, R1-R5, A and G. Mode S is saved by S5 (server opens its wrap). In mode E the server has no key: it commits, advances the head, publishes. Every replica derives M', fails P4, keeps its old head and refuses the record; every later legitimate epoch has prev = hash(bad record) and is refused by C2 too. The group is frozen at every replica until a backup-key recovery epoch, and the server cannot tell (its chain verifies). service-rekey has the same hole.
findings.fix: For any record claiming dek_gen = head.dek_gen whose (c0, wraps) differ from head's, require a link proof that the author's own wrap in head and in the new record open to the same M: Chaum-Pedersen with witness a_author proving log_B(A_author) = log_{(c0_head - c0_new)}(c_author_head - c_author_new); 64 bytes, 2 scalar mults to verify; base is non-identity whenever r is fresh; the author is a recipient of both by A2+G1. For service-rekey (author = old service key, not in the new wraps) use the two-witness variant proving A_old = a_old*B, A_new = a_new*B, c_old_head - c_new_new = a_old*c0_head - a_new*c0_new (96 bytes). Head proof + new proof + link makes M = M' checkable with no key, which is what R4 claims today. Hash the link commitments into the FS transcript under a distinct domain string. Until then, rewrite R4's rationale and add an EpochRefused{group, hash} report from replicas so the wedge is visible.

findings.title: dek_gen is reissued after a recovery re-root; DEK caches, group_dek rows and the AAD keyed by dek_gen collide
findings.detail: C3 jumps epoch on recovery because replicas may be ahead of a restored database, but dek_gen does not jump: R4 lets a recovery with fresh M set dek_gen = restored_head.dek_gen + 1. Scenario: replicas at epoch 9 / gen 5; DB restored to epoch 7 / gen 3; recovery with fresh M' at epoch = now, dek_gen = 4. Replicas re-root (P2) and hold gen 4 = M' while their group_dek table already has (group, 4) from the old timeline with a different M, and any DEK cache keyed (group, dek_gen) - the key the design specifies for mode S - returns the stale key. The next rotate produces gen 5 a second time with a third M. 'dek_gen +1 whenever M changes' no longer identifies a key; apply rule 3's group_dek insert hits a PK conflict; a replica with a gen-keyed cache fails every AEAD after the recovery - it goes dark exactly at disaster-recovery time. The AAD (binds dek_gen, not the record) is byte-identical across the two timelines. No confidentiality break, but a silent availability failure in the one path the design exists to make safe.
findings.fix: A recovery with fresh M MUST set dek_gen = the recovery record's epoch (same max(head+1, now) jump) so a generation number is never reissued with a different M; a recovery keeping M keeps head.dek_gen. Key every DEK cache and the replica generation registry by (group_id, dek_commit) or hash(record), never dek_gen alone. Serving nodes MUST derive a DEK only from the head record and refuse to decrypt any secret_version row whose dek_gen != head.dek_gen - which also turns a re-inserted pre-rotate row (DB write) into a loud failure instead of stale plaintext served via an old record's retained wraps.

findings.title: Genesis is the unverified root: server-chosen pinned/acl plus an unspecified name<->group_id binding lets a hostile server still replace a group at replicas
findings.detail: Replicas key heads by group_id (P1) and accept any genesis for an unknown group_id (C1) with whatever backup/service keys it pins; the sync Group message carries a server-supplied name and nothing says what a replica does when a known name arrives with a new group_id. In mode S the server holds the service key and A1 lets it author a genesis with any acl and pinned set. A compromised authoritative node mints group_id Y, name 'prod', acl = {attacker admin, replica reader}, pinned = {backup: attacker key, service: server}, plus its own ciphertext; the replica has no head for Y, accepts, and - if it maps by name as today's replica tables do (secret_group.name UNIQUE) - its 'prod' is attacker-controlled: the exact forgery the threat-model delta says is excluded. Works without minting too: present any group where the replica reads and an attacker is admin under the victim name. Independently, 'the backup key is the only root' is uncheckable by a replica: P2 re-roots from 'its head's backup key', which for such a group is the attacker's. And S1 does not require a client-supplied genesis (CreateGroup{genesis}) to pin meta.backup_pubkey, so a service admin can create a group the operator's backup key can never recover.
findings.fix: (1) Replicas carry the operator's backup public key (and in mode S the service public key) in configuration and MUST reject any genesis whose pinned entries differ, accepting later backup-key changes only via recovery records extending an already-accepted chain. (2) S1 MUST require pinned == meta keys for every genesis, client-supplied or minted. (3) Replicas MUST bind name->group_id on first sight and refuse a different group_id under a known name; delete-and-recreate becomes an operator action on the replica, like P2's unknown-backup-key case. (4) Restrict server-minted genesis to migration; a live CreateGroup always carries the creator's signed genesis.

findings.title: A rotate may reuse an older generation's M; the != head.dek_commit check only looks one step back
findings.detail: R4 for rotate requires dek_commit != head.dek_commit and c0 != head.c0. An admin who wants to keep a kicked reader X reading chooses M_new = M_g for an earlier generation g in which X was a recipient (X still holds M_g or DEK_g). The record passes every verifier, the chain asserts 'X kicked, everything re-encrypted, authored by A', and X decrypts every later snapshot. Verifiable revocation fails in exactly the case it exists for, and unlike an out-of-band leak the chain positively asserts the opposite. Verifiers already hold the data to catch it.
findings.fix: Every verifier keeps the set of all dek_commit values seen for the group (32 bytes per generation; auditors have the chain) and rejects a rotate or recovery-with-rotate whose dek_commit has appeared before. No protocol change.

findings.title: Non-canonical, small-order and torsion-carrying EndpointIds are accepted at registration but can never be recipients
findings.detail: ed25519-dalek 3's VerifyingKey::from_bytes only requires decompression (verifying.rs:175-183); curve25519-dalek 5's decompress does not check canonicality; iroh's EndpointId parse adds nothing; server.rs add_identity parses and stores. A registered id can re-compress to different bytes or carry a torsion component, and still authenticates on the transport (dalek verify is cofactorless: a signer holding A' = aB + T succeeds whenever the challenge scalar is 0 mod 8, about one handshake in eight). E3 then rejects every record listing it: granting it read is an unfixable build failure, and the migration genesis for any group that already has such a reader in group_acl fails - migration step 2 does not say what happens to that group. Only chain points are E3-checked, so a torsion key can still be a service admin.
findings.fix: Validate at the boundary: AddIdentity, init (first service admin), the backup/service key files and the migration tool MUST reject a key that is non-canonical (decompress -> compress != bytes), the identity, or not torsion-free, with a clear error; migration MUST list such rows and refuse to run until removed. Keep E3 as second line; extend the promised negative tests from c_i to A_i, c0 and author.

findings.title: The rotate author re-supplies attribution fields; S5 does not verify put_sig, so plaintext can be swapped or signatures stripped during re-encryption
findings.detail: Section 4 steps 2-3 have the admin export (..., author?, put_sig?) and re-stage them 'verbatim'; the reencrypted digest does not cover them and S5 only checks that each staged row decrypts. A rogue admin (or buggy client) can (a) decrypt db-password, change the plaintext, re-encrypt, keep the original writer's put_sig - the server commits it with the writer's author column intact; readers later see a signature failure attributed to that writer and read it as corruption; or (b) stage put_sig = NULL for every row, silently downgrading the whole group to 'unverified' in one epoch. Neither is visible in the chain, which records only that A rotated.
findings.fix: The stage carries only (name, version, nonce, ciphertext); the server keeps created_at, created_by, author and put_sig from its own row and never accepts them from the stage. In mode S, S5 MUST verify put_sig over the decrypted plaintext for every row that has one and refuse the record on any failure. In mode E, readers MUST treat a put_sig failure as tampering by the author of the latest rotate, not corruption, and the sync spec should say so.

findings.title: Proof nonce k reuse across two proofs with different transcripts reveals r, hence M, to anyone holding both records
findings.detail: s = k - e*r. Two proofs sharing k under different e (any transcript change: an added recipient, a re-staged c set) give r = (s1 - s2)/(e2 - e1), then M = c_i - r*A_i for any listed recipient: the DEK becomes computable from the records alone. The CAS-loser path invites this: 'the loser refetches the head, rebuilds (its ACL edits reapplied on top ...) and resubmits'. A rebuild that keeps r and M (an acl epoch whose recipient set grew in the race) but re-runs the prover from retained state, or derives k deterministically from r alone, yields the two-transcript pair; the losing submission already reached the server, which is not trusted for confidentiality in mode E and may retain or audit it.
findings.fix: k MUST be fresh from OsRng per proof, or derived RFC-6979-style from (r, the complete FS transcript) so a transcript change forces a new k; r MUST be zeroized immediately after the first proof so any rebuild must re-randomise. State this in section 2 next to the r/m zeroization rule.

findings.title: Zeroization and constant-time requirements are stated for r and m only
findings.detail: Values whose leak reveals the DEK also include k, M on both prover and reader, the HKDF PRK K, the reader's intermediate a*c0, the M.compress() buffer, the Scalar from to_scalar(), and the mode-S per-(group, gen) DEK cache, which keeps plaintext DEKs resident for the process lifetime where today's server unwraps per request and drops (crypto.rs Dek is ZeroizeOnDrop; a long-lived cache defeats that). The design specifies vartime for verification but nothing for the prover (k*B, k*(A_i - A_1), r*A_i, e*r) and decryptor (a*c0), which operate on secrets; vartime there leaks r or a through timing on a shared host.
findings.fix: Prover and decryptor MUST use curve25519-dalek's constant-time operators, never the vartime_* family; wrap k, r, m, M, K, a*c0 and compress buffers in Zeroizing; bound the DEK cache (derive per request, or an LRU with explicit zeroize on evict and on epoch change).

strengths: Cofactor discipline is correct and necessary: ed25519-dalek 3's to_scalar() returns the clamped AND reduced scalar (signing.rs:547-554), so a mod l has arbitrary residue mod 8 and a reader cannot rely on clamping to cancel torsion; E3 on c0, every c_i and every A, applied by every verifier including replicas (P1), with exact full-group verification and no cofactor multiplication, is a complete answer. curve25519-dalek 5's is_torsion_free is a genuine l*P test (edwards.rs:1435). A torsion component in c0 or c_i would pass the proof with probability 1/8 per grind and give per-recipient M + a_i*T; the design excludes it at the input.

E2 strict byte ordering plus the recompress check yields distinct points, so A_i - A_1 is never the identity; c0 = identity (r = 0, M public) is rejected by the non-identity rule; n = 1 (backup key as sole reader) degenerates safely to a Schnorr proof on c0 with no split view possible.

The single-(e, s) batched proof is sound: special soundness with one common witness over prime-order bases, HVZK, strong Fiat-Shamir (statement points, n, group_id, dek_gen, domain string, SHA-512 -> from_bytes_mod_order_wide). Omitting epoch/prev from the transcript is harmless because the signature binds the proof to the record and a transplanted true statement stays true.

ElGamal malleability is moot: the signature covers c0, every wrap and the proof, and any change to a c_i changes the FS challenge so the proof fails without r. Domain separation was checked against every iroh 1.0.3 signing site - relay challenge (32-byte blake3-derived value), TLS-export auth (16 bytes), TLS CertificateVerify (0x20-padded), pkarr (bencode) - none can satisfy E1's exact parse of an epoch or put message.

DEK and dek_commit as two HKDF-Expand outputs of one PRK salted by a random group_id: the commit is binding on M, reveals nothing usable about the DEK, is unlinkable across groups, and makes the non-committing-AEAD argument sound within one record because the proof leaves no second key to use.
verdict: The proof system as specified (multi-recipient ElGamal on Edwards25519, batched Chaum-Pedersen, E2/E3/E4 point hygiene, strong Fiat-Shamir, signature over a fixed layout) is sound; every cofactor, encoding, duplicate, n=1, transcript and domain-separation probe in the lens came back handled and was verified against the pinned dalek and iroh sources. The breaks are around the proof: what a keyless verifier can actually conclude (M continuity across acl/service-rekey is only an author's claim, so mode E can be wedged by one bad record; the genesis root is server-chosen and replicas neither pin the operator's keys nor bind names to group ids), generation numbering that is not unique across a recovery re-root, and rotate freshness checked only one step back. Adopt with four mandatory changes before implementation: the link proof, the dek_gen jump on recovery with commit-keyed caches, replica key pinning plus name binding, and the dek_commit history check. Boundary validation of EndpointIds, server-owned attribution columns with put_sig verification in S5, and the nonce-reuse / zeroization / constant-time rules are implementation requirements that belong in the spec text.
